mentions.name: Penteglot
mentions.description: A fork of Emacs's Eglot LSP client that adds multi-server support, allowing multiple language servers to run simultaneously for the same buffer (e.g. basedpyright or pyrefly plus ruff for Python, or ts-ls plus eslint and tailwind servers for TypeScript). Still work-in-progress, with the hope of being merged into Emacs one day.
mentions.problem: Eglot lacked multi-server support, which was one of the main reasons people stuck with lsp-mode over Eglot.
mentions.audience: Emacs users and developers who need multiple language servers per buffer
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on Penteglot - a fork of Emacs's Eglot LSP client with multi-server support.

The main feature: you can run multiple language servers simultaneously for the same buffer.
